aidb_assessment.novelty: The main novelty is systems-level localization of the read boundary in existing agent-memory services, combined with empirical separation of evidence compatibility, role completeness, canonical publication agreement, availability, and recovery admission. The mechanisms themselves adapt established snapshot, lock, and sequence-counter ideas; the contribution is their end-to-end placement and evaluation across heterogeneous recall stages.
aidb_assessment.rationale: The controlled comparisons, exhaustive request accounting, separate failure study, and explicit negative results support the central claim within the tested scope. AIDB should treat it as strong evidence for whole-recall protection and publication-aware recovery, but not as sufficient evidence to adopt a particular policy across production systems because the workload, ownership model, fault model, and semantic evaluation are narrow.
aidb_assessment.usefulness: High for designers of memory, retrieval, and provenance services whose responses span multiple connections or stores. The paper provides actionable contracts and exposes why naive repetition and local consistency checks are insufficient. Production selection between Gate and Epoch still requires workload-specific latency, concurrency, crash, and multi-worker testing.

executive_summary: The paper shows that protecting only an initial database operation is insufficient when an agent-memory recall performs later enrichment or materialization. Across controlled and open-arrival tests, whole-call locking and optimistic epoch validation prevent mixed-version Cognee evidence; a shared PostgreSQL snapshot fixes Hindsight’s cross-connection mismatch. Epoch trades shorter update tails for longer recall tails, while a persistent DIRTY state converts uncertain post-failure content into explicit refusal until recovery. The evidence is unusually careful about completeness, canonical publication, queues, and failed updates. Adoption should remain conditional: tests use one changing source, deterministic representations, one owner process, selected fault sites, and no downstream answer-quality evaluation.

assumptions: The evidence checker’s captured receipts and source relationships are sufficient to classify compatibility within the tested source scope.
All relevant writers and background publication work participate in the selected protection scope, which has one owner process.
The six-role representation contract is an appropriate completeness target for the evaluated Cognee workload, but it is not a proxy for answer quality.
The tested stores safely tolerate the read/write overlap permitted by Epoch, while separate lifecycle guards protect resource lifetime.
key_components: A compatibility predicate asks whether every current-state evidence item can be explained by one dependency-consistent source state; unresolved or empty evidence is labeled UNKNOWN.
Cognee completeness requires passage, summary, city and employer graph assertions, and city and employer fact text. Usability additionally requires timely and compatible delivery.
Gate holds shared read permission through awaited search and full materialization, while a writer holds exclusive permission through update and completion checks.

Epoch records a healthy READY generation, performs and materializes the native recall, then validates that the same generation remains healthy; crossed reads are discarded and retried within the original deadline.
Failure handling preserves a DIRTY state after failed or uncertain admitted mutations and explicitly refuses recall until successful recovery establishes a newer READY generation.
method.overview: For Hindsight, the wrapper exports one read-only PostgreSQL Repeatable Read snapshot and imports it into every participating connection before its first query, keeping the exporter open through recall completion. For Cognee, the study compares ordinary recall, unconditional whole-call repetition, a writer-preference read/write lock held through materialization, and optimistic generation validation. Epoch readers accept a fully materialized response only when the generation remains the same, healthy, and even; failed or uncertain protected mutations leave the scope DIRTY until a successful later operation reopens it. Controlled interleavings, open-arrival workloads, and injected failures are evaluated with direct source bindings and backend receipts used for checking rather than response construction.

open_questions: How do Gate, Epoch, and shared snapshots behave under realistic multi-source updates, heterogeneous document sizes, nondeterministic extraction, and production embedding dimensions?
Can generation and health metadata be made safe across multiple workers and every background publisher without introducing a new single point of failure?
Would build-then-swap provide a better availability and latency envelope once storage duplication and old-generation reclamation are included?
Which caller classes should receive strict DIRTY refusal, and which can safely consume a typed DEGRADED response with publication status and missing-role metadata?
How robust are recovery guarantees under process crashes, cancellation races, snapshot-import failures, and failures during the recovery operation itself?
Do evidence-consistency repairs measurably improve citation correctness, answer quality, or audit outcomes in downstream agent tasks?

problem.importance: Contradictory evidence undermines citation and audit, while locally coherent derived content after failure may still disagree with the canonical record. A repair must therefore distinguish compatibility, completeness, freshness, availability, and recovery rather than report only successful retrieval.
problem.scope: The study examines complete-recall protection in Hindsight and Cognee, including enrichment and lazy-result materialization, normal incremental and full-rebuild updates, selected update failures, service refusal, and recovery. It does not evaluate downstream model quality or establish behavior for multiple owner processes.
problem.statement: A memory service may assemble one response through multiple reads or stores. If an update occurs between those reads, the returned assertion and its cited source may belong to different revisions; an update failure can also leave derived and canonical state published differently.

proposed_experiments.baseline: Single-owner Epoch and multi-worker unprotected recall under identical multi-source update and recall traces.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: A shared, durable generation protocol preserves the zero-delivered-conflict property of Epoch across multiple worker processes and background publishers without materially reducing usable service.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Usable-by-deadline fraction, accompanied by delivered-conflict fraction and recovery time after worker termination.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop adoption if any protected response has incompatible source bindings, if a worker crash permits READY while publication is incomplete, or if usable-by-deadline service is worse than the single-owner baseline by more than a predeclared margin.

proposed_experiments.baseline: Gate and Epoch under the same spaced, burst, and injected-failure schedules.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Build-then-swap reduces recall-tail inflation and DIRTY refusal time relative to Gate and Epoch while retaining compatible, complete evidence.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Usable-by-deadline fraction across all scheduled recalls, with storage amplification and update-p95 as required secondary constraints.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop if any mixed-generation response is delivered, old-generation resources are reclaimed before all readers finish, or the predeclared storage or update-tail budget is exceeded.

proposed_experiments.baseline: Strict DIRTY refusal and unprotected native delivery after the same injected failures.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: A typed DEGRADED response after failed publication improves task availability without misleading callers when canonical disagreement and missing roles are explicit.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Downstream source-attribution accuracy on audit tasks, reported jointly with completed-task fraction.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop if DEGRADED responses reduce attribution accuracy relative to strict refusal, conceal canonical disagreement, or fail to improve completed-task fraction by the predeclared minimum.

It remains partial because the artifact was not inspected here, Hindsight cost-environment details are missing, and no independent reproduction is reported.

The supplied blocks do not report an independent artifact reproduction or cross-host replication.
The natural-language statement of artifact availability does not establish artifact completeness, executability, or archival permanence.

results.context: This is the strongest natural-load correctness comparison. It shows that incremental publication can preserve role coverage while still mixing revisions, whereas both whole-call protection strategies eliminate delivered incompatibility in the tested workloads.

evidence.quote: 199 of 12,010 scheduled recalls with spaced writes (1.66%) and 284 of 12,010 with bursts (2.36%).

results.result: In open-arrival default-update workloads, ordinary recall produced 199 conflicting responses among 12,010 scheduled recalls for spaced writes and 284 among 12,010 for bursts; Gate and Epoch each delivered complete, compatible responses for all 24,020 scheduled recalls.

results.context: This consequential negative result rules out a superficially simple retry policy. The repeated call had no checker, backoff, or fallback, so it could cross the same publication window again.

results.result: For Hindsight, sharing one PostgreSQL snapshot removed the controlled mismatch in all ten pairs, but median native-read p95 rose from 19.09 to 28.97 ms. The joint cost screen failed because the one-client recall-rate ratio was 0.790 against a 0.80 threshold.
